summary: The user_id-is-None guard clause was moved to run after the lookup(user_id) call instead of before it; whether that changes observable behavior for a missing id depends on lookup's own handling of None, which is not shown in this diff.

items.title: Guard clause now runs after the lookup call
items.before: get_active_user checked user_id is None and returned before calling lookup.
items.after: get_active_user calls lookup(user_id) first, then checks user_id is None.
items.statement: The guard clause that returns None for a missing user id was moved after the lookup(user_id) call, so lookup now runs unconditionally before that check runs.

items.title: Effect of calling lookup with a None id is unclear
items.statement: Whether calling lookup(None) now raises an error or has a side effect cannot be determined from this diff alone, because lookup's implementation is not defined or shown anywhere in this change.

items.title: Return value contract for resolved lookups is unchanged
items.before: A resolved lookup returned None for an inactive or missing record and the record otherwise, after the guard and validity checks.
items.after: A resolved lookup still returns None for an inactive or missing record and the record otherwise; only the order of the two leading statements changed.
items.statement: For any user_id where lookup completes without raising, the final return contract is unchanged: only the order of the two leading statements changed, not the trailing checks or return statements.
